name: Town Hall Hotel (Da Terra, Restaurant Elis)
summary: A boutique hotel in a restored Edwardian building on Patriot Square in Bethnal Green, home to the Michelin-starred restaurant Da Terra.

music.notes: Offers seasonal events, Christmas parties and private or corporate events.

crowd: The hotel says it caters to business travellers, city explorers and people after a unique London escape.

evidence.quote: Set within a beautifully restored Edwardian building in the heart of Bethnal Green
Da Terra — Michelin Starred Restaurant in London
Located inside the landmark Edwardian Town Hall Hotel, Da Terra has an elegant and contemporary look
we offer an unforgettable stay for business travellers, city explorers and those seeking a unique London escape.
Whether you’re planning a Christmas party, private celebration or corporate event
join us for one of our seasonal events and celebrations
Town Hall Hotel is one of East London’s most distinctive luxury boutique hotels
Patriot Square, Bethnal Green, London, E2 9NF
The building began life in 1910 as the Bethnal Green Town Hall, later expanded in the 1930s with an elegant art‐deco wing.
After decades of municipal use, it was restored and reimagined as a hotel in 2010.

Guests enter through a grand marble lobby, where original Edwardian features, polished stone, ornate plasterwork, and a sweeping staircase sit comfortably alongside contemporary art and modern furnishings.
Our luxurious 14 metre, heated swimming pool and newly-refurbished gym are open to guests every day.

history.change: profile created from the 13 October 2026 venue research
added story (opened, then, now, vibe, worth knowing) from Travelling for Business and the venue's own sites

story.then: According to Travelling for Business, the building gained an art deco wing in the 1930s. Once its council days were over, it was restored and turned into a hotel in 2010.
story.now: The venue's own website says guests have a heated 14 metre pool and a gym. Its restaurant Da Terra is led by chef Rafael Cagali, who has Brazilian and Italian roots, and the restaurant's own website says to allow about three hours for the full experience or two for the three-course lunch.
story.vibe: Travelling for Business describes a marble entrance hall with the building's Edwardian features, stonework and plasterwork and a sweeping staircase, set beside modern furnishings and contemporary art.
worth_knowing: Films and TV shot here include Atonement, Snatch, Poirot, Brideshead Revisited and Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, says the venue's own website.
The venue's own website names the Council Chamber and the marble staircase among its filming spaces.
